text: One sinking ship's anchor knocked out about a quarter of the internet traffic through the Red Sea!
Why does that matter to me?
Because almost everything you send between continents travels through cables on the sea floor. Satellites carry under one percent.
About six hundred cables carry over ninety-nine percent of that data.
What happened in the Red Sea?
In twenty twenty-four, a cargo ship hit by a Houthi missile drifted, dragging its anchor, and cut three cables.
In twenty twenty-five, more were cut near Jeddah. And in the Baltic, cable after cable has been damaged since twenty twenty-three.
More and more, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon. They use about three quarters of all international bandwidth.
Like, follow History Sketches, and tell us what we should map next!
And all it took to hit a quarter of the Red Sea's traffic... was one anchor.
